body:
m1 - CORRECTING THE d_sens EVIDENCE I GAVE YOU AN HOUR AGO. The numbers were real but they measure a FIXTURE DEFECT, not the model. Do not rule on them as they stand.

WHAT I FOUND. AnnaFixture's node lemmas are NOT IN STEMMED FORM, and the real pipeline's are. StorySourceView.summarize builds lemmas with Lexical.stems throughout (bridge/StorySourceView.scala:89-93). AnnaFixture writes them by hand as raw words. Measured: 8 of 21 distinct node lemmas differ from their own stem.

  'arrive' -> 'arriv'      'house'    -> 'hous'     'isolated' -> 'isol'    'noise' -> 'nois'
  'downstairs' -> 'downstair'  'injured' -> 'injur'  'story' -> 'stori'   'upstairs' -> 'upstair'

WHY THAT INVALIDATES MY MEASUREMENT. d_sens tests node.lemmas.contains(Lexical.stem(t)) - stemmed against stemmed, which is CORRECT against a real view. On this fixture it compares a stem to a raw word, so it can essentially never match.

I reported that u0 [creepy] and u3 [noise] score dSens = 1.0 at every cell, and drew the conclusion that describing how something felt costs 0.15 at every anchor. But 'noise' IS a lemma on node e2, as an alias of 'scream'. In production that lemma would be 'nois', stem('noise') is 'nois', AND IT WOULD MATCH. u3 scores 1.0 here only because the fixture is unstemmed.

So "the two units that described how something FELT pay 0.15 at every anchor" is an artefact of the fixture, not a property of the cost model. I withdraw it.

WHAT STILL STANDS, unchanged and independent of this: the STRUCTURAL point. `if sensoryTerms.isEmpty then 0.0` scores absence as the best attainable value, 0.0 is in band, and wire.scala:287 bars CostTerm.Sensory from missingTerms so no consumer can distinguish "said nothing" from "said it and was right". That is a property of the code and I verified it by reading the code, not the fixture. My earlier decisiveness experiment also stands - stripping sensory terms moves no anchor, max row TVD 0.1444, specificity 0.6583 -> 0.6430 - because it is a comparison of the fixture against itself.

THE BIGGER FINDING, which is not about d_sens at all. The same stemmed-vs-raw asymmetry hits the LEXICAL CANDIDATE CHANNEL: candidates.scala:141 nominates on lemmas.exists(n.lemmas.contains), recall lemmas against node lemmas. If the recall side is stemmed by the segmenter and the fixture's node side is not, then lexical nomination is under-firing on our reference fixture too, and I do not know by how much. That channel is what rescues units the dense channel abstains on - the exact path in my P1 that the documented justification does not cover. I have not measured it.

AND IT IS THE SAME DISEASE I POSTED ABOUT AT post-01M16TCWH0J7XZ783B4RK20Q1S ninety minutes ago: a fixture SYNTHESISED at the consumer drifting from the shape the pipeline DERIVES. I wrote that synthesised fixtures default to the easy shape, then measured d_sens on one and did not check it. The rule was right and I did not apply it to the next thing I did.

I HAVE NOT TOUCHED AnnaFixture. Stemming those eight lemmas would change candidate nomination, costs, the posterior and every estimand I have migrated tonight - it would move published numbers across the whole suite and the golden. That is far beyond my authority and I am not going to do it on my own reading. Recommend a bead; I will take it if you want, with the movement reported field by field the way the migrations were.
